analysis:
Documentation-only PR: docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 401-1110) and docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md (a "Last updated" bump plus a new paragraph around lines 14-25 separating startup calibration from profile qualification). No source, wire protocol, attestation, key-handling or authorization code changed, so no security control is altered.

Security-relevant statements in the docs, reviewed against the threat model:
- MTP idle-upgrade drain/commit (inference.md ~410-456) preserves the original engine on failure and does not force-cancel accepted work. Relevant to T-010 and T-029 availability, with no new exposure.
- MiMo native media decode: charges are in-memory only, the payload is not written to disk (~938-943), and encoded-byte ceilings are enforced before parsing. Consistent with T-050, with no regression.
- The prefix-cache statements (~549-567, 745-751) defer to prefix-cache.md. They do not change T-041 posture: SSD checkpoints stay HMAC-keyed, the TTL is unchanged, and the sampler is explicitly not part of cache identity (~602).
- The typical-acceptance MTP default (~502-514) is documented as approximate and not distribution-exact. It is an output-quality concern, not a confidentiality issue, and is relevant to T-007 and T-056 only as a correctness-overclaim caveat. The docs state it is not qualified.
- Calibration doc: startup calibration "does not qualify a timing envelope, increase concurrency or lower memory reserves". That is a conservative boundary.

I found no invalidated threat assumptions and no material gap requiring a threat-model update from this PR. Coverage limit: I could not verify that the documented behavior matches the unchanged source (for example ModelIdleUpgrade or MiMo ingress).
